clue.text: Assignations on Palm Beach?

definitions.meaning: the fruit found hanging on a date palm, with the Florida resort as a pun

explanation.surface: Romantic meetings arranged at the Florida resort.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: romantic appointments, and the sweet brown fruit borne by a palm tree.

clue.text: Clever little birds

parts.note: a dab hand is a skilled person, so dab means expert
chicks are young birds

explanation.surface: Praise for some bright small birds.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines small grebes, and its parts build them: DAB (expert, as in 'a dab hand') and CHICKS (little birds).
explanation.definitionFit: Small diving grebes common on British ponds and lakes.

clue.text: What one expects to get on, fatigue duty?

definitions.text: What one expects to get on, fatigue duty?

parts.words: What one expects to get on, fatigue duty?
parts.note: fatigue duty is menial military labour; doing it leaves a soldier worn out

explanation.surface: A soldier asking what to expect on a spell of fatigues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fatigue duty' is a soldier's spell of menial work; the result of that is exhaustion.
explanation.definitionFit: Worn out and weary after hard work.

clue.text: Pudding which, in a way, is no meal

indicators.note: the fodder is changed in some fashion, so its letters come out rearranged

explanation.surface: A dessert that, oddly, doesn't count as a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a way' rearranges IS NO MEAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Semolina boiled with milk and sugar is a British school dessert.

clue.text: Lake for a bath perhaps? Ask a Canadian

indicators.note: perhaps marks the letters of the words before it as only one possible arrangement, so they are shuffled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A traveller asks a local which lake would do for a bath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges A BATH into ATHAB; then ASK and A follow as written. 'Canadian' adds that the lake is in Canada.
explanation.definitionFit: Lake Athabaska is a large freshwater body in western Canada.

clue.text: Singer has a retreat in Scotland

annotationWithheld.why: Singer has a retreat in Scotland (4): no parse found giving ALTO from 'has a retreat in Scotland'
annotationWithheld.clue: Singer has a retreat in Scotland

clue.text: Those who do it have their own convictions

definitions.text: Those who do it have their own convictions

parts.words: Those who do it have their own convictions
parts.note: convictions means criminal sentences, not firm beliefs

explanation.surface: People of principle who act on their beliefs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'convictions' seems to mean beliefs; here it means court convictions, and the work is a prison punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: Heavy manual work imposed on prisoners as a sentence.

clue.text: Entreat a person to scram

parts.note: to entreat is to plead
one means a person, as in 'one should'

explanation.surface: Pleading with someone to clear off.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned command to go away, like 'off with you'.

clue.text: Select cap that's eccentric, for show

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or out of line, so the letters are put into an odd order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Picking an odd hat to put on a display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's eccentric' rearranges SELECT CAP.
explanation.definitionFit: A striking public display or performance.

clue.text: Articled offspring of an old navigator

parts.note: given an article: the indefinite article is put in front
a son is a child

explanation.surface: A trainee lawyer descended from an early sailor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Articled' suggests a trainee solicitor; here it means 'with the article', AN. George Anson was an 18th-century British admiral who sailed round the world.
explanation.definitionFit: Admiral George Anson led a famous voyage around the globe in the 1740s.

clue.text: Its readers look for the weather forecast

definitions.text: Its readers look for the weather forecast

parts.words: Its readers look for the weather forecast
parts.note: the readers are not of a newspaper but people who read a dial to predict the weather

explanation.surface: Newspaper readers turning to the weather page.
explanation.walkthrough: 'readers' suggests a newspaper; here they are people taking a reading from an instrument that measures air pressure.
explanation.definitionFit: An instrument measuring atmospheric pressure is read to predict coming weather.

clue.text: Delightful songs

parts.note: part-songs for unaccompanied voices, whose name also means delight or joy

explanation.surface: A compliment paid to a choir's music.
explanation.walkthrough: The name of these unaccompanied part-songs is also a word for joy, so they are 'delightful' in name.
explanation.definitionFit: A glee is an English part-song for three or more voices; the word also means mirth.

clue.text: Secret conference — how to' achieve togetherness

definitions.meaning: crowding close together in a tight group

explanation.surface: A conspiratorial meeting described as a recipe for unity.
explanation.definitionFit: A whispered private talk, and also the act of crowding tightly together.

clue.text: On pirate's fateful path, not returning-food for the fishes

parts.note: pirates made victims walk the plank

indicators.note: returning means the word for not is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A doomed captive walking the plank, never to return, ends up as fish food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns NOT into TON, which follows PLANK. Victims of pirates were made to 'walk the plank'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiny drifting organisms in the sea are the staple diet of many fish.

clue.text: Deem models out of order, not minding their own business

indicators.note: out of order means not in sequence, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Judging fashion models as nosy busybodies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of order' rearranges DEEM MODELS.
explanation.definitionFit: Interfering in other people's affairs; nosy and prying.

clue.text: Royal race in China?

parts.note: the crown stands for the monarchy
the Derby is a famous English horse race at Epsom

explanation.surface: Asking whether there is a royal horse race held in China.
explanation.walkthrough: China here means porcelain: Crown Derby is a make of fine English porcelain. The Derby is a famous English flat horse race.
explanation.definitionFit: Crown Derby is a brand of English porcelain tableware, which is called china.

clue.text: Forthright, but not in oral form

definitions.meaning: read as two words: out, not, and spoken, said aloud

explanation.surface: Someone frank, yet who does not speak.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition splits the answer: OUT means not, and the rest means said by mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: Candid and blunt in speech; split, it also says 'not voiced'.

clue.text: Part of a Russian capital vessel

indicators.note: only a portion of the city name is used, with its opening letters dropped

parts.note: Moscow is the capital of Russia

explanation.surface: A section of a vessel built in Moscow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part of' drops MO from MOSCOW, leaving the boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A scow is a flat-bottomed boat used for carrying cargo.

clue.text: Whereby we get a measure of power in current affairs

definitions.text: Whereby we get a measure of power in current affairs

parts.words: Whereby we get a measure of power in current affairs
parts.note: current affairs means electric current, not the news; power is electrical

explanation.surface: Judging political influence in the news of the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'power in current affairs' sounds political; here it means electrical power, measured in watts.
explanation.definitionFit: An instrument that measures electric power in a circuit, in watts.

clue.text: It ensures there are no grounds for complaint

definitions.text: It ensures there are no grounds for complaint

parts.words: It ensures there are no grounds for complaint
parts.note: grounds means coffee dregs, not reasons

explanation.surface: A reassurance that nobody will have cause to grumble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grounds for complaint' means a reason to object; here the grounds are coffee dregs, kept out of the cup.
explanation.definitionFit: A sieve or filter that holds back coffee or tea leaves.

clue.text: The building position

parts.note: the plot of ground where construction stands or will stand

explanation.surface: A plain statement about where a structure goes.
explanation.definitionFit: The location of a building or planned construction is its plot.

clue.text: It's made by regulation

parts.note: regulation here means tuning or setting a mechanism, not rule-making

explanation.surface: A remark about rules made by authorities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regulation' suggests official rules; here it means regulating a clock or machine, which makes a fine change to it.
explanation.definitionFit: Regulating a device, such as a watch, involves a small corrective change.

clue.text: We hear mineral water' may be measured in them

definitions.text: water' may be measured in them

indicators.note: we hear marks a word that is said, not spelt

parts.note: quartz is a common crystalline mineral

explanation.surface: A remark about how mineral water is sold by volume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'We hear' makes the mineral QUARTZ sound like QUARTS, units of a quarter of a gallon. 'mineral water' looks like one phrase, but it splits.
explanation.definitionFit: Units of liquid volume, each a quarter of a gallon.

clue.text: How a cause may be embraced without a single worry ?

definitions.text: How a cause may be embraced without a single worry ?

parts.words: How a cause may be embraced without a single worry ?
parts.note: a cause one supports is said to be taken up wholeheartedly; read again, someone no longer single has gained a spouse

explanation.surface: Taking up a cause with no anxieties at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without a single worry' seems to mean carefree; read as 'not single', it means married, hence having a spouse.
explanation.definitionFit: To adopt or support a cause is to take it up; the word also means married.

clue.text: Not quite enough for the breakfast dish in Surrey

indicators.note: falling short means one letter of the dish is missing

parts.note: ham and egg, here as egg ham

explanation.surface: Complaining that a portion of breakfast in Surrey was too small.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not quite enough for' drops one G from EGG HAM. Egham is a town in Surrey, a county south-west of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Egham is a town in the English county of Surrey, near Windsor.

clue.text: Just the job for a back-seat driver

definitions.text: Just the job for a back-seat driver

parts.words: Just the job for a back-seat driver
parts.note: the driver of this horse-drawn cab sat high up behind the passengers

explanation.surface: Mocking a passenger who keeps telling the driver what to do.
explanation.walkthrough: A back-seat driver is usually a nagging passenger; in this two-wheeled horse cab, the driver literally sat behind.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-wheeled horse-drawn cab whose driver sat on a raised seat at the rear.

clue.text: Speak gushingly

parts.note: to talk at length, pouring words out like a jet of water

explanation.surface: Talking in an effusive flow.
explanation.definitionFit: To declaim at length; also a jet of liquid gushing out.

clue.text: Don't go for support

definitions.meaning: a prop, such as a rope steadying a mast

explanation.surface: Begging someone to remain and help.
explanation.definitionFit: Remain behind, and also a prop or brace, as in a ship's rigging.

clue.text: A pleasure tramp ?

parts.note: tramp means a long walk, not a vagrant; this person walks for fun

explanation.surface: A vagrant who enjoys life on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tramp' suggests a vagrant; here it is someone who goes on long country walks for enjoyment.
explanation.definitionFit: A rambler who walks long distances in the countryside for recreation.

clue.text: Thorough, but one more needed for a hat-trick

parts.words: but one more needed for a hat-trick
parts.note: in cricket, a hat-trick is three dismissals in a row; the phrase holds 'out' twice, so one more would make three

explanation.surface: A cricketer who has taken two wickets needs one more for a hat-trick.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a hat-trick is three wickets with consecutive balls; the answer contains the word for a dismissal twice, one short of three.
explanation.definitionFit: Complete, utter, in every respect: an absolute or total example.

clue.text: Most yearn madly for such seclusion

indicators.note: madly signals that the letters of the two words before it are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Most people long desperately for a life of retreat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'madly' rearranges MOST YEARN.
explanation.definitionFit: A religious house where monks live apart from the world is a place of withdrawal.

clue.text: Two-way helicopter lift

indicators.note: the word reads the same in both directions, forwards and backwards

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A helicopter flying both ways to lift passengers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two-way' says the answer reads the same either way.
explanation.definitionFit: The spinning blades on top give a helicopter its lift.
